title: Sortable employee table, end to end
summary: Add column sorting to a paginated employee list: new query params on the handler, an ordering that holds across every page, and table headers that toggle it.

checkpoints.title: The handler accepts sort and direction
checkpoints.hint: listEmployees already takes a query object. Add sort and dir to it, with sensible defaults.

checkpoints.title: Sorting happens in the database, not after pagination
checkpoints.hint: If you sort the rows you already fetched, page 1 is only the first page re-ordered. The ORDER BY has to be in the query, before LIMIT.

checkpoints.title: An unknown sort column is rejected, not interpolated
checkpoints.hint: Map the incoming string to a real column through an allowlist. Never build the ORDER BY from raw input.

checkpoints.title: Clicking a header sorts, and clicking again reverses it
checkpoints.hint: The header click has to change local state and pass it to the fetch, and clicking the active column flips the direction.

checkpoints.title: The rules hold on rosters nobody wrote
checkpoints.hint: These rosters walk every column in both directions, at a page size chosen not to divide the roster, which is the walk the other four never take. Read the first line of the report, because it names the rule that broke. If an employee is on no page at all, look for a WHERE that is only there when the sort column is nullable. If the ordering breaks across a boundary, check that the key the database sorted on is the column the caller asked for: an allowlist keyed `started_at` never matches a request for `startedAt` and falls back to name without saying so.
